title: Normalized total derived internal condensed invariants
statement: For a commutative condensed ring $R$ on the small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [def-weil-size-convention], use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and the sectionwise internal action category and normalized fixed-section adjunction of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. The bundled coefficient, section modules, abelian-structure specification and scalar-action specification are those of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. For every topological group $J$ (not necessarily profinite), equip its action category with the Grothendieck abelian structure induced by the action site [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Let $\Gamma_{R,J}$ be its normalized invariant subsheaf: its inclusion is injective on every test object, with image the sections fixed after every profinite base change, and both transpose formulas use that inclusion. In the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], set $F_{R,J}=R\Gamma_{R,J}$ to be the total right derived functor with its canonical computation unit; $L_{R,J}=D(T_J)$ is exact trivial inflation and the adjunction is the canonical derived adjunction. For $u:H\to J$ continuous, $U_u=D(u^*)$ is termwise exact restriction. Define $b_u:F_{R,J}\to U_uF_{R,H}$ by deriving the unique underived invariant inclusion, normalized on every complex by the computation units. The identity restriction comparison is induced by identity maps of underlying modules. For a condensed ring map $\varphi:R\to R'$, let $s_J,s_0$ be the exact scalar restrictions normalized by their underlying-module comparisons. The invariant/scalar isomorphism is the unique one commuting with invariant inclusions. Its canonical total-derived comparison $d_J:F_{R,J}s_J\simeq s_0F_{R',J}$ is fixed by the computation-unit equation on every complex. For $f:N\to s_JN'$, define $c_J(f)=F_{R,J}(f);d_J(N')$. The scalar/group commutation isomorphism is fixed on underlying modules and then localized. All shifts are the canonical signed shifts. No coefficient flatness is assumed.

proof.text: Partial stage-3 proof: trivialAdditive and restrictionAdditive hold because both functors retain the original morphisms and their addition. The private forgetReflects lemma constructs the inverse of an equivariant isomorphism from its underlying inverse, using equivariance and the two inverse equations on every section. Given forgetExact, forgetting reflects finite limits and colimits; the composites of trivial action and group restriction with forgetting are respectively the identity and the original forgetful functor. Apply preservesFiniteLimits_of_reflects_of_preserves and its colimit analogue. For scalarExact use ScalarAction.underlying to identify the composite with forgetting followed by exact internal scalar restriction. This proves trivialLimits, trivialColimits, restrictionLimits, restrictionColimits and scalarExact.

Construct invariantRestrictionExist by restricting the normalized G-invariant adjunction counit along v and transposing through the H-invariant adjunction. Naturality is naturality of the G-counit and the H-hom equivalence. The normalized transpose equation identifies its composite with the H-inclusion with the G-inclusion. For uniqueness apply the inverse H-hom equivalence and the normalized untranspose formula; the prescribed inclusion equation then forces the same underlying equivariant arrow.

Apply the existing functorial flat-resolution instance for sheaves to abelian groups on the coherent profinite site; abelian groups have the flat separator Z. This closes sheafFlatResolution. The existing additive and canonical-shift instances for the total right derived functor give derivedProperties.

For groupMapShift, the canonical derived adjunctions for trivial action and invariants commute with shifts. Their right-derived computation units therefore commute with shifts. The pullback auxiliary transformation is a composite of termwise natural transformations, signed-shift-compatible factorization comparisons and the H-computation unit, so commutes with shifts. The universal right-derived factorization identifies this transformation with the G-unit followed by the localized group map. The G-unit is invertible on K-injectives, which represent every derived object; NatTrans.CommShift.of_comp_whiskerLeft_Qh therefore proves shift compatibility of groupMap. The exact computation-unit equality groupMapNormalization is the existing rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ_rightDerivedPullback_app theorem.

Construct identityActionExist with NatIso.ofComponents of identity maps: precomposition of the action by the identity continuous monoid homomorphism is the original action. Any other comparison with the prescribed underlying components equals it by Iso.ext, natural-transformation extensionality and Subtype.ext.

Still open in this partial delivery: actionAbelianData, actionGrothendieck, forgetExact, invariantsExist, degreeZero, scalarActionExist, scalarInvariantsExist, scalarComparisonExist, scalarGroupExist and scalarComparisonShift. Their unchanged theorem docstrings give the original action-site, fixed-submodule, scalar, degree-zero and derived comparison arguments. No step is replaced by a renamed hypothesis or a new sorry.
